Microbiological Research.title: The antioxidant mitoquinone potentiates polymyxin activity against multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae via dual targeting of membrane phospholipids and fatty acid biosynthesis.
Microbiological Research.abstract: There is an urgent need for strategies to counter antimicrobial resistance (AMR), especially among carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE). In this study, MitoQ's potential to be utilized as a polymyxin adjuvant was explored. MitoQ alone potently inhibited Gram-positive bacteria (MICs 1-4 µg/mL) but showed weak activity against Gram-negative strains (MICs ≥ 16 µg/mL). When combined with polymyxins, MitoQ acted via a dual-target mechanism to enhance killing and reverse resistance in Enterobacteriaceae. In susceptible strains, MitoQ bound inner-membrane phospholipids, phosphatidylglycerol (PG) and cardiolipin (CL), synergizing with polymyxin-mediated outer-membrane disruption to rapidly compromise membrane integrity. In resistant strains carrying phoQ/pmrB mutations or mcr-1, membrane targeting alone did not restore sensitivity. Instead, DARTS (Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability) methodology identified FabH, the key enzyme in the type II fatty acid synthesis (FASII) pathway, as a direct MitoQ target. Inhibition of FabH by MitoQ shifted lipid composition, decreasing saturated-to-unsaturated fatty acid ratios, and increased membrane fluidity, thereby resensitizing bacteria to polymyxins. In murine peritonitis and abscess models, co-administration of MitoQ and polymyxin B achieved > 90% reductions in bacterial load and bioluminescence compared to monotherapy. These results demonstrate that MitoQ restores polymyxin efficacy through combined membrane lipid disruption and FabH inhibition, highlighting its potential as an adjuvant to combat multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.

Science Bulletin.title: Extinct spreading ridges as transient plate boundaries: seismic evidence from the South China Sea.
Science Bulletin.abstract: Extinct spreading ridges preserve critical records of former plate boundaries and the processes that shape oceanic crust. The South China Sea, characterized by brief and spatially heterogeneous seafloor spreading, serves as a natural laboratory for investigating extinct ridge evolution. Yet the interaction between this former boundary and regional tectonics, and the variations in crustal accretion across the sub-basins, remain incompletely understood. Using data from 28 ocean bottom seismometers in the South China Sea basin, we applied teleseismic P-to-S receiver function analysis with an improved H-κ stacking method that incorporates dynamic velocity scanning and waveform coherence assessment to enhance the robustness of crustal thickness and Vp/Vs ratio estimates. Crustal thickness mostly ranges from 5 to 9 km within the basin, with the thinnest (4.0 km) crust near the ridge axis and the thickest (11.3 km) beneath a seamount. The bulk crustal Vp/Vs ratio varies from 1.68 to 2.26, with values of 1.72 to 2.04 along the extinct ridge, indicating variations in crustal composition and internal structure. In the Southwest Sub-basin, we image a thickened crust-mantle transition zone in the off-axis region, suggesting magmatic underplating or intrusion. These observations, interpreted in the context of variable magma supply, tectonic extension, and pre-existing continental architecture, point to a complex ridge extinction process in the South China Sea. This study provides new constraints on the crustal architecture and evolution of extinct ridges in marginal basins.

Water Research.title: Microbial transformation and defluorination of PFAS under diverse redox regimes: Evidence, mechanisms, and functional implications.
Water Research.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are generally resistant to biodegradation, yet increasing evidence indicates that selected PFAS undergo microbial transformation and, in some cases, C-F bond cleavage. However, our current understanding is fragmented across different microbial systems and electron acceptor conditions, and a conventional oxic-anoxic classification does not adequately resolve these condition-specific differences. Here, we review microbial transformation and defluorination across oxic, nitrate-reducing, sulfate-reducing, iron-reducing, methanogenic, Feammox, and mixed-reducing conditions. This review encompasses 103 PFAS structures, of which 74 were transformed under at least one tested condition. Across these studies, transformation rates, product profiles, and defluorination varied among electron acceptor conditions, including for the same or structurally related PFAS. However, differences in inoculum, microbial biomass, and primary-substrate supply across studies limit direct comparisons and prevent these variations from being attributed solely to electron acceptor conditions. These findings suggest that PFAS molecular structure alone does not fully explain the reported variability, while the specific contributions of electron-accepting processes and microbial activities remain unresolved. We further distinguish parent-compound loss from evidence of C-F bond cleavage and evaluate complementary information provided by parent-compound loss, transformation products, and fluorine mass balance. Previous studies have shown that microbial associations and protein annotations can be used to identify candidate microorganisms and proteins, but these candidates still require validation against the corresponding PFAS. This review provides an electron acceptor-resolved framework for evaluating the biotransformation of PFAS and identifies controlled cross-condition experiments, rigorous fluorine accounting, and direct microbial and biochemical validation as priorities for assessing PFAS biodegradation potential.

Water Research.title: Rethinking anammox self-enrichment: Ecological selection, metabolic plasticity and engineering opportunities.
Water Research.abstract: Although anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) represents a cornerstone of low-carbon nitrogen removal, its full-scale deployment remains constrained by the reliance on scarce, externally cultivated seed sludge and the frequent ecological maladaptation of bioaugmented biomass. In situ anammox self-enrichment offers a transformative paradigm shift from exogenous biomass transplantation to the directional selection of indigenous anammox bacteria (AnAOB). Unlike routine anammox acclimation or process enhancement, anammox self-enrichment uses in situ regulation. It wakes up and selectively enriches native AnAOB without relying on external seeding. However, insights into self-enrichment remain fragmented across isolated operational studies, lacking a unified mechanistic framework. Here, we critically review AnAOB self-enrichment by bridging ecological selection, metabolic plasticity, molecular regulation, and engineering control. We first elucidate how multidimensional environmental filtering, substrate partitioning, and initial inoculum legacies define the realized niches for rare AnAOB proliferation. Beyond canonical lithoautotrophy, we highlight how mixotrophic flexibility and alternative energy-conserving pathways-particularly extracellular electron transfer coupled with iron, sulfur, manganese, or conductive materials-Provide crucial metabolic buffering during transient nitrite starvation. At the molecular level, interspecies quorum sensing and the transcriptional reprogramming of central nitrogen-carbon cascades orchestrate the transition from low-abundance persistence to functional dominance. Translating these principles into practice requires multi-pressure synergistic engineering that integrates sustained nitrite supply-demand matching (especially via partial denitrification), spatial retention (granulation and biofilms), selective chemical inhibition, and material-assisted stimulation. Finally, we propose a roadmap integrating ecological theory, single-cell and multi-omics technologies, and artificial intelligence to advance anammox self-enrichment from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive trajectory forecasting and intelligent mainstream implementation.
